chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar and others from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding
a man who entered into ihram while wearing a shirt, he said: 'He removes it without cutting it, and if he wore it after entering ihram, he cuts it and removes it from what is below his feet.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.قَمِيص: A shirt or tunic, one of the specific garments forbidden to men in ihram
key_terms.مِمَّا يَلِي رِجْلَيْهِ: From what is below/adjacent to his feet
key_terms.يَشُقُّهُ: He cuts it (referring to the garment)

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if he enters ihram while wearing a shirt?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between wearing a shirt before versus after entering the state of *ihram*, a key detail in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of the garment. It establishes that if the shirt was already on the body at the moment of *ihram*, it is removed intact (by unbuttoning or pulling), whereas if donned subsequently, it must be cut to avoid the prohibition of wearing sewn garments. This ruling reflects the broader principle of maintaining the simplicity of the pilgrim's attire while ensuring practical compliance with the sacred state.
